newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Jan 3.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Jan 3.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- President Fidel Ramos placed a war on crime and poverty at the top of his list of "must-do" projects for the remaining 18 months of his term. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)
- The country's premier business club, the Makati Business Club, has formally asked Defense Secretary Renato de Villa to run for president in 1998, a reliable source said. (INQUIRER)

- Proponents of the Constitutional amendments to lift the term limits of elective officials, including that of the President's, asked the Supreme Court to dissolve the restraining order that stopped them from garthering signatures for a people's initiative. They cited an existing law that gives power to the people to propose amendments to the Constitution. (BULLETIN).
- President Ramos cancelled the bidding for a container port terminal at Subic Bay, one of the country's largest privatisation projects, and ordered the process started anew. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)
- The government is predicting a better consolidated public sector financial position in the next two years after an estimated deficit of 790 million pesos in 1996. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)
- The Bureau of Internal Revenue directed the imposition of a 20 percent final tax on reverse repurchase papers despite strong opposition by the Central Bank. (ALL NESPAPERS)
- The Department of Agriculture expects production of unmilled rice to grow 5.3 percent to 12 million tonnes this year compared to 11.4 million tonnes last year. (STAR)
